KEY MESSAGE 1...

A ridge of high pressure will remain in place today and lead to dry 
and pleasant conditions. Once the fog clears this morning, skies 
will be sunny as temperatures will climb into the upper 70s to mid 
80s. Dew points will only be in the 50s, so humidity will be low. 
Overnight, temperatures will fall into the 50s and low 60s. With 
light winds and mostly clear skies, fog is expected to develop 
once again. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...

While the ridge will still be in place come Wednesday, models are 
showing a wave or two riding this ridge. Dry air in place looks to 
keep things dry early in the day. With the high pressure just off 
the coast, the flow around the high will advect moisture northward 
over the region Wednesday afternoon, supporting showers and 
thunderstorms as the waves move through. Models differ on the 
solutions as the GFS has been consistent with conditions staying dry 
with a wave moving through earlier in the day. Also, there is some 
question on the amount of instability and whether or not a cap 
holds. Either way, this forecast will favor the majority of most 
guidance and keep chances for showers and storms present.

Moisture increases Thursday as a weak disturbance approaches the 
region and eventually moves through. PWATs will approach 2 inches 
over the region. In addition, MLCAPE is modeled to be 1000 to 1500 
J/kg. Flow in the mid-levels will be fairly weak though strong 
enough for 0-6 km bulk shear to be 20 to 30 kts. Conditions will be 
favorable for thunderstorms to develop and a few strong ones cannot 
be ruled out. DCAPE values are high in model soundings, though weak 
low-level flow would suggest that there won't be much for winds to 
mix down. Still, given the high PWAT values and rich moisture, it 
may be possible to get wet microbursts. Seeing the long, skinny 
CAPE, small hail may also be possible. Of course, with this moisture-
rich system, the main concern would be locally heavy rainfall and 
isolated flash flooding. The AHPS total precipitation accumulation 
over the last 7 days is 200 to 400% above normal across parts of the 
region, especially in the Twin Tiers and Catskills Regions. Despite 
a couple of dry days, it likely will not be enough for significant 
improvements to the antecedent conditions leading up to Thursday.

The broad trough over the Central US will drift east as the high 
pressure slides further out to sea. As this trough moves into the 
region, it flattens with flow becoming more zonal. Another 
disturbance will move through to support another round of showers 
and thunderstorms with conditions very similar to Thursday. With 
high PWATs, fairly high instability, and modest shear, the same 
hazards will be in place. Based on GFS soundings, there may be 
potential for slower moving showers on Friday into Saturday. For 
both days, WPC has had a Marginal Risk for excessive rainfall and 
that is likely to continue throughout the week. 

Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms will be possible this 
weekend, though forcing will be weaker and moisture is bit more 
limited. Remaining in the zonal flow, a wave moves through on 
Saturday. With drier air moving in, the heavy rain potential will be 
limited as PWATs are modeled to be lower. Instability will be 
present though shear may be weak, so confidence is low for the 
potential of stronger storms at this time. A weak frontal boundary 
then sweeps through on Sunday with another round of showers, though 
there is uncertainty with the timing. Then as we enter early next 
week, there is no change to the overall pattern, so Monday will 
continue the streak of consecutive days with chances for showers in 
the forecast.

Throughout this period, conditions will be warm and humid. Highs 
will be in the 80s and lows will be in the 60s. For early August, 
this near average though some days may be slightly above. Heat index 
values in the 90s will be possible in the valleys at the end of the 
week. Depending on the timing of showers and the amount of cloud 
cover during the daytime hours, temperatures may be slightly cooler 
than forecasted.
